bracket: [Textbook misprint: the book's worked solution prints the field inside the toroid as \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i}{2uR}\), with an italic Latin \(u\) where \(\pi\) belongs. The line before it, \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i}{2\pi r_0}\), and the flux line after it both carry \(2\pi\), and putting \(r_0 \cong R\) gives \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i}{2\pi R}\). The working above has been corrected. The final answer is unaffected.]

[Textbook misprint: the book's worked solution substitutes the length of the solenoid as \(20 \cdot 10^{-4}\) m. The question gives \(l = 20\) cm, which is \(20 \cdot 10^{-2}\) m \(= 0.20\) m, and the book's own result needs that value: \(L = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times (200)^2 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}}{0.20} = 1.257 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{H} = 0.1257\) mH. With \(20 \times 10^{-4}\) m the same expression would give 12.57 mH, a hundred times larger. The substitution above has been corrected. The final answers are unaffected.]
